title: Exclude only common invariant subspaces with finite Fourier support
statement: Suppose a nonzero common invariant finite-dimensional space has a FINITE union of Fourier supports. Choose a support mode with k_i=n!=0 and transversej!=i, then maximize k_j in that fixedn slice. The complex combination B_ij^c+iB_ij^s=P[e^(2pi i x_j)partial_i] creates the unique shifted coefficient at k+e_j outside the finite union. The preceding projection lower bound prevents its coefficient vanishing, contradiction. This excludes precisely finite-Fourier common invariant spaces; it does not exclude a general smooth/H1 finite-dimensional invariant space with infinite Fourier support or provide any quantitative relaxation/mixing/compiler.
